sections.label: Government Motion on FTAs
sections.summary: The Government moved a separate Motion to explain its position on FTAs and foreigners, and is prepared to fight the next election on this issue.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: His Motion appears to be addressing concerns about jobs, but it, yet again, falsely attributes the challenges faced to our FTAs and foreigners.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: This is despite the clarifications made by my colleagues Mr Ong Ye Kung and Dr Tan See Leng in July.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: That is why the Government has moved a separate Motion to explain and reiterate our position on this important matter.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: It is important Singaporeans, and the world, understand where we stand.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: And as Mr Ong Ye Kung said in July, we are prepared to fight the next election on this issue.

sections.label: PMETs share of local workforce
sections.summary: PMETs now make up 60% of Singapore's local workforce.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Today, PMETs make up a much larger 60% of our local workforce.

sections.label: Median income growth 2010-2019
sections.summary: From 2010 to 2019, median income in real terms grew 3.2% per annum for residents.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: From 2010 to 2019, up until COVID-19 struck, median income in real terms grew by 3.2% per annum for residents.

sections.label: Local PMET employment growth
sections.summary: Between 2010 and 2020, local PMET employment grew by about 300,000.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Between 2010 and 2020, local PMET employment grew by about 300,000.

sections.label: PMET vacancies today
sections.summary: There are more than 25,000 PMET vacancies today, with many companies still looking to hire.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: First, we already have more than 25,000 PMET vacancies today, with many companies still looking to hire.

sections.label: Foreign PMETs in workforce
sections.summary: Today, foreign PMETs account for about 20% of the PMET workforce.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Today, foreign PMETs account for about 20% of our PMET workforce.

sections.label: GDP and median salary growth
sections.summary: GDP per capita rose from around $35,000 in 1995 to more than $80,000 now, and median resident salaries from under $2,000 to around $4,500.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In 1995, that is the earliest I could get data on, our GDP per capita was just around $35,000 instead of more than $80,000 now.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: And median salaries of residents were less than $2,000 compared to around $4,500 today.

sections.label: Unfilled tech jobs estimate
sections.summary: IMDA estimates around 19,000 tech jobs go unfilled across the economy each year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: IMDA estimates there are around 19,000 unfilled tech jobs across our economy each year.

sections.label: Singaporeans in senior finance roles
sections.summary: The number of Singaporeans holding senior level positions in the financial sector has grown steadily and continues to do so.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Across the financial sector, the number of Singaporeans holding senior level positions has also grown steadily over the years and continues to do so.

sections.label: PMET retrenchments and employment
sections.summary: Over the past decade there were around 60,000 resident PMET retrenchments but around 300,000 more resident PMET employment.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: For example, over the past decade, we have had around 60,000 resident PMET retrenchments.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: But we have seen a much bigger increase of around 300,000 in PMET employment for residents.

sections.label: Fair employment guidelines into law
sections.summary: The Tripartite Guidelines on Fair Employment Practices will be enshrined into law to signal zero tolerance of workplace discrimination and give agencies more regulatory levers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: As the Prime Minister announced at NDR, we will now enshrine the Tripartite Guidelines on Fair Employment Practices into law.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We were concerned that doing so would lead to a more litigious and confrontational process; it could easily sour workplace relations, harming both employers and employees.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: But after hearing from the Labour Movement and NTUC Members of Parliament, and consulting our tripartite partners, we decided we could manage these concerns and that it was time to change, to send a clear signal that we have zero tolerance of discrimination at the workplace and to give our agencies more regulatory levers to take action against errant employers.

sections.label: SkillsFuture and mid-career PMETs
sections.summary: The Government is investing heavily in SkillsFuture, with special attention to mid-career PMETs, to help Singaporeans stay employable and find new jobs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We understand your concerns and will do our utmost to help you.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: This is why the Government has been investing heavily in SkillsFuture to help all Singaporeans learn for life and to stay employable in this competitive environment.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We are paying special attention to mid-career PMETs to equip them with relevant skills and to find new jobs.

sections.label: Career Conversion Programme hiring
sections.summary: A company hired a new industry worker under the Career Conversion Programme, valuing his attitude and past experience.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Although he was new to the industry, his company valued his good attitude and past experience and hired him under the Career Conversion Programme.

sections.label: COVID-19 accelerates worker support
sections.summary: COVID-19 drives faster industry transformation, higher wages and productivity, and more employment and training support for displaced, mid-career and mature workers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: COVID-19 has given us greater impetus to accelerate this important work and to provide more help for displaced workers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We are pressing ahead with our industry transformation efforts to raise wages and productivity across all sectors.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We are stepping up employment and training support, especially for mid-career and mature workers to help them pivot into new growth areas.

sections.label: Permanent shift in support levels
sections.summary: After the crisis, support levels are expected to shift permanently with more help for workers amid greater volatility and disruption.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: After the crisis, we expect a permanent shift in support levels with more help for our workers, especially as we enter a period of greater volatility and disruption.

sections.label: Singapore talent policy
sections.summary: Singapore has a talent policy to maximise its overall talent pool for the best outcomes for Singapore and Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: What we have is a Singapore talent policy – to maximise our overall talent pool, so that we can achieve the best outcomes for Singapore and Singaporeans.

sections.label: EP qualifying salary raised
sections.summary: Last year, the EP qualifying salary was raised twice.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Last year, we raised the EP qualifying salary twice.

sections.label: FTAs and CECA explained
sections.summary: Two Ministers explained why FTAs including CECA attract investments and jobs, and why Movement of Natural Persons provisions do not allow free foreign access.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: At the last debate in July, my colleagues Mr Ong Ye Kung and Dr Tan See Leng explained why we need FTAs, including CECA, to attract investments and create jobs for Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Both Ministers went to great lengths, showing the specific clauses in the text, to explain why the Movement of Natural Persons provisions in our FTAs do not allow free access for foreigners to work in Singapore.

sections.label: Ong Ye Kung questions PSP on CECA
sections.summary: Ong Ye Kung asked whether the PSP agreed that FTAs including CECA are fundamental to Singapore's survival and are not the cause of PME challenges.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In particular, at the last debate, Mr Ong Ye Kung asked whether the PSP agreed on two key points: first, that FTAs, including CECA, are fundamental to Singapore's economic survival and our ability to earn a living and we should not shake this bedrock principle for political purposes; second, that CECA is not the cause of the challenges faced by our PMEs and does not allow a free flow of Indian PMEs into Singapore.

sections.label: PSP accused over CECA rhetoric
sections.summary: The passage says if the PSP does not acknowledge FTAs are not the cause of PMET challenges, CECA is a cover to stoke racist and xenophobic sentiments.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: If he acknowledges that FTAs, including CECA, are not the cause of the challenges faced by our PMETs, then we can put this issue to rest once and for all.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: But if he continues to equivocate, or to make misleading or false claims, then we can only conclude that CECA is a cover for the PSP to stoke racist and xenophobic sentiments.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The business community here has already expressed concerns about the rhetoric against foreigners and FTAs – they are worried that the PSP's anti-foreigner stance will undermine their access to workers and jeopardise their overall operations here.

sections.label: Open economy measures for workers
sections.summary: Singapore stays open and connected to create jobs while taking measures on worker inflow, workplace discrimination and displaced workers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We stay open and connected to the world to create more jobs and uplift everyone.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We take concrete measures to deal with the downsides of an open economy, manage the inflow of workers, tackle discrimination at the workplace and look after those who are displaced.
